content:
To my horror, I have discovered that someone with 4 gigs of ram on their laptop wants to do the Imperial formalizing course which starts in 4 months. I think that we are going to have to offer some kind of central server to such people, hosted at Imperial, accessible via an Imperial login, where they will be able to open the course repo (which will be a standard Lean 4 repo depending on mathlib) and make their own files.

My instinct is to start solving this problem now. Does anyone have any advice on how we might set this up?
Is getting imperial to pay for github codespaces an option (assuming they are not free already for you)?

I suspect rubbing a magic lamp and saying "please setup https://github.com/leanprover/lean-workbench on some cloud machine for me" will solve your problems at this point. (And 4 months is sufficiently far in the future that everything will work nicely by then.) If you already have a suitable machine already available, you won't even have to tell the genie your credit card number. :-)
There is https://prove.reaslab.io/home developed by Peking University but I'm not sure if it can be self-hosted.
